rfi.title: Macron toughens stance on arson as wildfires sweep France
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has said there would be "zero tolerance" for arson after France was hit by wildfires that have scorched thousands of hectares. Dozens of people have been arrested across the country over starting fires deliberately or by accident as multiple intense heatwaves since May have dried out forests and fields.

rfi.title: Greenpeace demands halt to Dangote's $17bn Kenya coastal refinery

rfi.title: French parliament passes assisted dying law after years of wrangling

rfi.title: Students in Cameroon protest new financial requirements for French visas
rfi.description: Dozens of people took to the streets outside the French embassy in Yaoundé this week to protest new rules that require Cameroonian nationals to demonstrate the means to pay tuition fees in full before they can obtain a student visa for France. Protesters say the policy will make studying in France impossible for many people who already have places at French institutions for the coming academic year.

rfi.title: EU and Ukraine seal drone deal to pair industry with battlefield expertise
rfi.description: European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday announced a drone deal with Ukraine to boost joint production of the key battlefield technology.

rfi.title: Lawyers vow to fight on after Kenya court rejects Rastafarians' cannabis bid
rfi.description: In a long-awaited ruling, Kenya's High Court has rejected a bid by Rastafarians to be allowed to smoke cannabis as part of their religious worship. But lawyers say the fight continues and the case has opened up debate on the country's drug laws and what constitutes religious freedom.

rfi.title: Firefighters tackle flare-ups in Fontainebleau forest after reining in blaze
rfi.description: Around 800 firefighters were still at work in Fontainebleau forest on Wednesday morning, tackling flare-ups after the fires were brought under control the previous day, following 48 hours of intense firefighting.

rfi.title: Ebola cases in DRC may be four times official tally, says WHO
rfi.description: The true number of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo is at least double, and possibly four times, the official tally, the World Health Organization's emergencies chief said on Tuesday. Official figures say the fever has infected nearly 2,000 people since mid-May.

rfi.title: France marks 10 years since Bastille Day terror attack in Nice killed 86

observador.title: IL: Montenegro deve avaliar "condições" do ministro
observador.description: Liberais consideraram que, se o processo das notas dos exames falhar, o primeiro-ministro deve reavaliar as capacidades de Fernando Alexandre. IL já fez um requerimento de toda a documentação.

observador.title: As notícias das 15h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: África do Sul detém 8.896 imigrantes em 14 dias
observador.description: Forças de segurança dizem que "números refletem o compromisso do Governo de agir com firmeza" contra imigração ilegal e crimes. País atravessa onda de ataques xenófobos contra migrantes africanos.

observador.title: Festival Tomorrowland regressa à Bélgica
observador.description: 200 mil pessoas por fim de semana e 38 mil visitantes no parque de campismo são as expectativas da organização do festival. Portugal marca presença no cartaz oficial com 6 artistas.

observador.title: Testosterona em soldados americanos. Hipocrisia ou inovação?
observador.description: O Secretário da Defesa dos Estados Unidos anuncia um novo programa de terapia de reposição de testosterona para os soldados masculinos do exército norte-americano. Médicos e Democratas criticam.

observador.title: Prisão preventiva para detido por ligação a rede de tráfico
observador.description: O homem de 49 anos detido em Lisboa por suspeita de integrar uma rede de tráfico de droga para os Açores. É um cidadão estrangeiro, de 74 anos, que transportava 14 quilogramas de haxixe.

observador.title: Festival Política em Lisboa, Coimbra, Loulé e Torres Vedras
observador.description: O Festival Política tem uma programação que inclui espetáculos, filmes, exposições, oficinas e visitas guiadas. A entrada é gratuita e esta edição é dedicada à Constituição da República Portuguesa.

observador.title: Lixo em praias alentejanas transformado em obras de arte
observador.description: Projeto intitulado "Waste 2 Arte" vai estar em exposição em Porto Covo, Sines. Pretende sensibilizar pessoas para "persistência de práticas poluentes" na região. Tem apoio do município e do ICNF.

observador.title: APAV apoiou mais de 200 turistas vítimas de violência
observador.description: Número de turistas apoiados aumentou 210,3% desde 2021. Maioria do sexo feminino. Violência doméstica é o crime registado, seguido de crimes sexuais. Foi apresentada queixa em 66% das situações.

observador.title: Crimes relacionados com jogo em Macau aumentam 12,2%
observador.description: Casos aumentam devido a câmbio ilegal de moeda. Autoridades apreenderam cerca de 1,9 milhões de euros em dinheiro e fichas. Crimes violentos sobem 4% em relação ao período homólogo.

observador.title: Governo da Madeira aponta a "desenvolvimento económico"
observador.description: O objetivo do Programa do Governo Regional é o desenvolvimento económico. Para que seja possível erradicar a pobreza e as desigualdades sociais.

observador.title: Tribunal confirma julgamento da mulher de Pedro Sánchez
observador.description: Begoña Gómez foi acusada de corrupção e apropriação indevida. Tribunal devolve passaporte e Gómez pode viajar. Continuam as "acusações populares" à família de Sánchez e ao PSOE.

observador.title: PAN anuncia recurso da decisão do TC que invalida reeleição
observador.description: O PAN anuncia que vai recorrer para o plenário do Tribunal Constitucional da decisão que invalidou a última eleição dos órgãos nacionais do partido. O tribunal declarou ilegal parte do regulamento.

spiegel.title: Wadym Jermolajew: Opfer von Anschlag in Monaco bezichtigt Kyjiws Geheimdienst HUR
spiegel.description: Wadym Jermolajew überlebte nur knapp die Explosion am Eingang eines Wohngebäudes. Jetzt erhebt er laut einem Schreiben schwere Vorwürfe gegen den ukrainischen Geheimdienst HUR und spricht von einem gezielten Mordversuch.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Die Entlassung des Verteidigungsministers stellt Selenskyj vor Probleme
spiegel.description: Mychailo Fedorow ist in der Ukraine höchst populär, als Verteidigungsminister hat er Innovationen gepusht und Korruption unterbunden. Dass Präsident Selenskyj ihn nun austauscht, sorgt für Proteste in Kyjiw – und Entrüstung in Berlin.

spiegel.title: Zendaya erklärt Hunter Schafer den »Interstellar«-Plot – und Tom Holland hat es gefilmt
spiegel.description: in den FIlmen von Christopher Nolan kann man schnell den Überblick verlieren. Gut, wenn man eine Freundin wie Zendaya hat, die helfen kann. Und zur Not die Handlungsstränge und Zeitachsen aufmalt.

spiegel.title: David Bowie: Im Herbst erscheinen unveröffentlichte Songs - mit Jimmy Page an der Gitarre
spiegel.description: Damals war er noch unbekannt und sang seine Nummern als Davie Jones ein. Nun erscheinen unveröffentlichte Studioaufnahmen von David Bowie – mit dem späteren Led-Zeppelin-Gitarristen als Gastmusiker.

spiegel.title: Schottland: Flächenbrand wütet in den Highlands
spiegel.description: In den Highlands in Schottland ist ein Feuer ausgebrochen. Über mehrere Kilometer soll sich der Brand bereits durch die Landschaft gefressen haben.

spiegel.title: Jens Spahn und die Leihmutterschaft in den USA: Warum der CDU-Politiker sich erklären müsste
spiegel.description: Der CDU-Politiker stellte sich jahrelang gegen Leihmutterschaftsmodelle. Nun sind Spahn und sein Ehemann über diesen Weg Eltern geworden. Das hätte er erklären müssen.

spiegel.title: Ukrainekrieg: Sigmar Gabriel bringt Angela Merkel als Vermittlerin ins Gespräch
spiegel.description: Ex-Vizekanzler Sigmar Gabriel bringt Angela Merkel mit Verweis auf das Minsker Abkommen erneut als Vermittlerin im Ukrainekrieg ins Spiel. Das Verhalten seiner eigenen Partei in der Koalition mit der Union finde er »lebensmüde«.

spiegel.title: Berlin bekommt von 2032 an Hunderte neue S-Bahn-Züge
spiegel.description: Die Hauptstadt erhält eine neue S-Bahn-Generation, barrierefrei und mit moderner Technik. Bis dahin müssen alte Züge saniert und aufgerüstet werden, und Pendler müssen sich auf Ausfälle und Umwege einstellen.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM: Diese Teams drehten entscheidende Spiele
spiegel.description: Zittern gegen Kap Verde, Rückstand gegen Ägypten und England: Dreimal retteten sich die Argentinier bei dieser WM nur knapp in die nächste Runde. Damit stehen sie in einer Reihe mit früheren großen Comebackteams.

spiegel.title: Göttingen: Knolle von seltener Titanwurz gestohlen
spiegel.description: Titanwurzen in Gewächshäusern faszinieren zahlreiche Besucher. Kein Wunder: Sie zählen zu den größten Blumen der Welt, blühen nur alle paar Jahre. In Göttingen haben sich nun Diebe für die Pflanze interessiert.

spiegel.title: AfD in NRW: Interne Chats befeuern Machtkampf um Alice Weidel
spiegel.description: »Alice Merkel«, »Terroristen«, »Schattenarmee«: Interne Chats geben Einblick in den eskalierenden Machtkampf der AfD in Nordrhein-Westfalen. Im Zentrum steht die Frage, ob Parteichefin Weidel in die Eskalation verstrickt ist.

spiegel.title: Algerien: Brand in Kinderheim – elf Menschen tot, mehrere Verletzte
spiegel.description: In einem Kinderheim in der algerischen Hauptstadt Algier ist ein Feuer ausgebrochen. Mehrere Menschen kamen ums Leben, darunter auch Kinder.

spiegel.title: Google muss Android-Handys für KI-Assistenten der Konkurrenz öffnen
spiegel.description: Wer ein Android-Handy besitzt, der muss einen KI-Assistenten auch dann per Sprachsteuerung öffnen können, wenn dieser nicht von Google ist. Dazu zwingt die EU-Kommission jetzt den Konzern. Der zeigt sich wenig begeistert.

spiegel.title: Evelyn Zupke: DDR-Hymne bei AfD-Veranstaltung in Dessau-Roßlau – SED-Opferbeauftragte spricht von »Verharmlosung«
spiegel.description: Uwe Steimle hat bei einer Veranstaltung die DDR-Hymne gesungen, AfD-Prominenz und Besucher stimmten ein. Für SED-Opfer sei das »unerträgliche« Geschichtsvergessenheit, kritisiert die Ombudsfrau Zupke.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News: Britische Regierung reagiert scharf auf Provokation argentinischer Spieler
spiegel.description: »Die Weltmeisterschaft ist nicht unsere, aber die Falklandinseln definitiv«: Downing Street hat seine Position zu den Falklandinseln bekräftigt. Und: Trump gibt im Finale sein WM-Debüt. Die News.

spiegel.title: Unwetter in Deutschland: Wie Hagel so groß wird wie Tennisbälle
spiegel.description: In mehreren Regionen Deutschlands sind riesige Hagelkörner eingeschlagen. Wie solche Eisbrocken im Sommer entstehen und wo das Risiko am höchsten ist.

spiegel.title: E-Scooter: Vor allem junge Fahrer verunglücken im Straßenverkehr
spiegel.description: Auf E-Scootern sind 2025 deutlich mehr Menschen verunglückt. Vor allem in Großstädten ist die Fahrt gefährlich. Fachleute fordern klare Konsequenzen.

spiegel.title: Bewerben mit KI: So nutzt du sie richtig
spiegel.description: Was eine Recruiterin über KI-Bewerbungen denkt. Was man allein auf einem Festival über sich lernt. Und wo Studierende am häufigsten noch bei den Eltern wohnen. Die Texte der Woche zu Studium und Berufseinstieg.

phys-org.title: A new record holder for the world's oldest amber discovered in China
phys-org.description: Paleontologists in China have discovered the oldest chemically verified amber ever found, dating to 385 million years ago. That's approximately 140 million years before dinosaurs roamed Earth. The previous record holder was an amber sample from the Late Carboniferous period, dating to about 320 million years ago.

phys-org.title: Webb telescope discovers hidden planet in famous star system
phys-org.description: Astronomers using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope have discovered a giant planet outside our solar system, called an exoplanet, hiding within one of the most intensely studied planetary systems in the Milky Way galaxy.

phys-org.title: Chemists shrink gallium nitride, the material behind LED lighting, into nanocrystals
phys-org.description: Nanocrystals are so useful that they formed the basis of the 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. But despite their usefulness, scientists have so far been able to make these microscopic crystals from only a limited palette of materials. A group of chemists at the University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory has announced a way to make nanocrystals from a useful class of materials known as metal nitrides—a previously impossible task.

phys-org.title: Listening to 'ringing' black holes unlocks future gravitational-wave astronomy
phys-org.description: Listening to the "ringing" produced by black holes after they collide and merge could allow scientists to test Einstein's theory of general relativity under the most extreme conditions in the universe while unlocking the secrets of these mysterious objects.

phys-org.title: New computational imaging method cuts X-ray dose while preserving high resolution
phys-org.description: Researchers have shown that it's possible to take clear, high-resolution X-ray images using very little radiation. With more development, the new approach could eventually make medical X-ray diagnostics less risky and more accessible.

phys-org.title: Hourly data reveal Alpine 100-year floods could arrive every 45 to 80 years
phys-org.description: Heavy precipitation becomes more intense with every degree Earth warms. This affects flooding. Using hourly data from 384 rivers in the Alps, researchers from the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF modeled how flooding will change by the end of the century. Their projections are significantly bleaker than earlier ones. The findings are published in the journal Science Advances.

phys-org.title: Researcher studies how people shift attention during everyday and high-stakes tasks
phys-org.description: Sustaining attention over long periods affects everything from routine tasks to high-stakes decisions. Whether it is an umpire making a split-second call or a driver glancing at a navigation system, even small lapses in focus can have meaningful consequences. New research from Texas A&M University is shedding light on how people allocate their attention and why it fluctuates in ways that can lead to both errors and improved performance.

phys-org.title: Scientists achieve all-electrical control of single-molecule quantum states
phys-org.description: Quantum technologies promise revolutionary advances in computing, sensing and information processing. However, controlling individual quantum bits (qubits) at the atomic scale remains a major challenge because conventional approaches rely on magnetic fields, which are difficult to confine to a single molecule.

phys-org.title: Cave-dwelling snail discovered in Greece, named after Hermes and the nymph who nurtured him
phys-org.description: A team of researchers from the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens has discovered a completely new genus and species of subterranean freshwater snail in the Peloponnese region of southern Greece. The species, Cyllena hermes, is a small, unpigmented, eyeless aquatic snail fully adapted to life underground.

phys-org.title: Rare Australian wattle is on the brink of extinction
phys-org.description: The spidery wattle (Acacia araneosa) is a national treasure. The plant is named for its spidery, leaflike phyllodes and shares the same iconic golden flowers as Australia's floral emblem, the golden wattle (Acacia pycnantha).

phys-org.title: A new 'library' for Feynman integrals
phys-org.description: Theoretical physicists at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) have developed a new method of ordering Feynman integrals. This critical step in making theoretical predictions for high-energy precision measurements has posed a major computational bottleneck until now.

phys-org.title: Americans increasingly view illicit drug policy through a partisan lens, new analysis finds
phys-org.description: Since the early 1970s, when the Nixon administration launched the "war on drugs," Gallup has been asking Americans how they feel about problems surrounding illicit drugs. But the war has not gone well and Gallup's surveys reflect the public's opinion on a drug crisis that has worsened over time.

phys-org.title: How ions flow like a liquid through a solid crystal
phys-org.description: A research team led by the University of Osaka, working with the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), RIKEN and the Institute of Science Tokyo, has uncovered a fundamental mechanism behind superionic conduction, in which ions move rapidly through a solid while its crystalline framework remains intact.

phys-org.title: Braided, exotic particles could build reliable, universal quantum computers
phys-org.description: A truly useful quantum computer must be able to run any algorithm, with the same versatility an ordinary laptop offers. Physicists have now shown a new way to give a quantum computer exactly that flexibility, harnessing the capabilities of exotic quantum particles called non-Abelian anyons.

phys-org.title: Quantum teleportation could reduce photon loss in long-distance communications
phys-org.description: Quantum technologies, which leverage the principles of quantum mechanics, have been found to outperform their classical counterparts on specific tasks. Among other things, past studies have highlighted the potential of quantum systems that can enable long-distance communication, using photons (i.e., particles of light) to carry quantum information.

phys-org.title: Natural peptide switches from calmodulin to the cancer-associated protein midkine depending on the ion environment
phys-org.description: Proteins regulate a wide range of biological processes inside and outside cells by binding to specific molecular partners. In recent years, short peptides that can selectively recognize disease-related proteins have attracted attention as compact molecular tools for biosensors, diagnostic technologies, and drug discovery. However, how such small peptides recognize different proteins depending on their surrounding chemical environment has not yet been fully understood.

phys-org.title: Genetic databases as the key to global benefit-sharing
phys-org.description: An international research team led by the Science Policy and Internationalization Department at the Leibniz Institute DSMZ-German Collection of Microorganisms and Cell Cultures has published a practical guide in the journal Scientific Data.

phys-org.title: Tiny gene edit cuts cadmium in rice by 48% without reducing yields
phys-org.description: Cadmium (Cd) contamination poses a serious threat to global food safety. As a toxic and carcinogenic heavy metal, cadmium can accumulate in agricultural soils through industrialization and urbanization before entering the human food chain. Rice is especially vulnerable because it absorbs more cadmium than other major cereal crops, making it one of the largest dietary sources of cadmium exposure for nearly half the world's population.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine

One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

proj-syn.title: The Death of the Degree
proj-syn.description: AI is often portrayed as a threat to higher education, with some administrators and professors focused on rooting out its use. But this approach fails to recognize that, in an AI-transformed world, the new dividing lines are technical capabilities and institutional pipelines that can quickly transform research into products.

proj-syn.title: Hungary’s Real Economic Test
proj-syn.description: Entering the euro with favorable market sentiment, but without an economy that can function well within a monetary union, would not serve Hungary’s long-term interests. It would be a formula for more broken promises—precisely the trend that the new government was elected to end.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Exposes the Global Economy’s Fault Lines
proj-syn.description: Buoyed by AI stocks, global financial markets have largely shrugged off the war with Iran. Yet the conflict’s long-term economic costs are only beginning to emerge, as depleted strategic oil reserves, damaged refining capacity, and rising fuel and fertilizer costs increasingly weigh on lower-income economies.

proj-syn.title: Governments Should Govern AI, Not Own It
proj-syn.description: AI systems are now powerful enough to threaten critical infrastructure, financial systems, and national security. Rather than becoming shareholders in AI companies, as US President Donald Trump has proposed, governments should invest in the independent institutions needed to hold the industry accountable.

proj-syn.title: The Tragedy of “Westalgia”
proj-syn.description: Some European leaders seem to think that abasing themselves for Donald Trump's pleasure is necessary to save NATO and keep the Western alliance alive. But by so desperately clinging to the good old days of the transatlantic relationship, Europe’s leaders are risking more than just their dignity.

proj-syn.title: The West’s Turkey Dilemma
proj-syn.description: Few countries better illustrate the difficult trade-off between democratic principles and strategic necessity than Turkey. As the country’s geopolitical and economic importance grows, NATO allies are becoming increasingly willing to overlook President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s attacks on democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: How the Tech Lords Hacked the Firm
proj-syn.description: A handful of tech oligarchs have figured out how to tap public markets without submitting to shareholder oversight. The recent SpaceX IPO represents the culmination of this process, granting Elon Musk near-total authority and revealing how thoroughly the mechanisms meant to hold corporate leaders accountable have been weakened.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Real Energy Test
proj-syn.description: The Iran war has underscored the fragility of global energy markets, exposing which economies can withstand repeated shocks and which cannot. For ASEAN+3 countries, resilience will depend on stronger electricity systems, regional cooperation, and institutions that can manage persistent uncertainty.

proj-syn.title: The US Economy Cannot Grow Without Renewables
proj-syn.description: Consumption demand, which has long powered America’s formidable economy, rests on the promise of cheap energy. But the Trump administration has conflated that with fossil fuels, confusing historic correlation with causation and, in the process, jeopardizing long-term prosperity.

proj-syn.title: The Purpose of Development Cooperation Is to Be Unnecessary
proj-syn.description: The original promise of development cooperation was to help countries overcome poverty, build productive economies, and reduce their dependence on external resources. That has not happened, and ongoing reviews of development cooperation, which focus on donor countries' needs and priorities, are unlikely to change this.

proj-syn.title: Oil Shocks Are No Longer So Shocking
proj-syn.description: Despite this year's US/Israeli-Iran war causing the largest-ever disruption to global oil supplies, the shocks of the 1970s had a greater impact. Because oil has been used as a weapon for so long, markets, policymakers, and strategists have adapted.

proj-syn.title: The Mother of All Economic Shocks Is Chinese Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Because analysts tend to put the United States at the center of the global economic story, they have overlooked the single most important force of the past 50 years. But it will be obvious to later generations that Chinese mercantilism has been more globally consequential than any other economic shock or policy choice.

proj-syn.title: Letting Russia Burn
proj-syn.description: From relentless Ukrainian drone strikes to soaring inflation and fuel shortages, Russia is paying an ever-higher price for Vladimir Putin's war of choice. But the war has become the organizing principle of Putin’s regime, leaving no path to lasting peace without a fundamental political transformation.

proj-syn.title: What AI Governance Demands
proj-syn.description: AI governance must account for everything from the technology’s material requirements to its effects on communities, businesses, labor markets, the environment, and strategic competition. To this end, a framework of verification-based trust—broader than national regulation and more flexible than a classic treaty—is essential.

proj-syn.title: A Japanese Wake-Up Call for America
proj-syn.description: Japan’s deepening currency and bond-market woes should be a wake-up call for other countries that appear to be on unsustainable fiscal paths, not least the United States, as well as France, Italy, and the United Kingdom. After all, a crisis in one country often draws investors' attention to others facing similar problems.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.
